resources.string: Choose what helps your translations. Each mode is independent; your entries stay saved when it is off.
Set preferred translations for names and recurring terms. Example: a game character always keeps the same name.
Reuse translations you corrected in a result card. Repeated phrases stay consistent.
Keep exact words on screen without translating them: sound effects, labels, or names you add yourself.
Optional built-in sound effects pack. Keeps matching Japanese captions unchanged; the full word list stays out of your glossary.
Choose a comfortable look. You can change it later in Settings.
Choose the language you read. Automatic source detection is usually enough.
Screen: start capture, open another app, then tap the floating button. Hold it for selection and other actions. Text and photos work from the app. Permissions are requested when needed.
Off: the button hides after 45 seconds of inactivity or when you close a translation card. Bring it back from the capture notification. Cards close after reading; Pin keeps one open.
The captured area is empty or protected. Allow capture of the whole screen, then retry. You can also share the message text to Clickn.
No text recognized. Select a larger area and check the OCR language. For Cyrillic, choose an OCR service that supports it or share the message text to Clickn.
Choose a ClicknTranslate logo for your home screen. Android may take a moment to refresh the icon.
